Load the libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
options(scipen = 999)

Data

For this homework, we are going to use the Gapminder data on population (pop), GDP per capita (gdp), and life expectancy (lex). These data were downloaded and compiled using the gapminder_compile.Rmd script in the data folder.

Let’s focus our attention on data from the past 100 years, between 1925 and 2025.

gapminder <- read_csv("data/gapminder.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(between(year, 1925, 2025))
  1. Use the function(s) of your choice to get an idea of the overall structure of the data, including its dimensions, column names, classes, etc.
glimpse(gapminder)

  1. Which five countries have had the largest absolute population growth between 1925-2025? Show this as a table.
pop_growth <- gapminder %>% 
  filter(year %in% c(1925, 2025)) %>% 
  select(country, year, pop) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = year,values_from = pop,names_prefix = "pop_") %>% 
  mutate(pop_growth = pop_2025 - pop_1925) %>% 
  slice_max(pop_growth, n = 5)

pop_growth

## 2 China     473741473 1416096094  942354621

  1. Make a plot that shows population growth over time for the top country you found in question #3.
gapminder %>% 
  filter(country == "India") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = pop)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue") +
  labs(title = "population growth over time",x = "yr",y = "pop") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1))

  1. Has global life expectancy changed between 1925 and 2025? Show the min, median, mean, and max for all countries (combined) in the dataset.
gapminder %>% 
  summarize(min_lex = min(lex, na.rm = T),median_lex = median(lex, na.rm = T),mean_lex = mean(lex, na.rm = T),max_lex = max(lex, na.rm = T))
## # A tibble: 1 × 4
##   min_lex median_lex mean_lex max_lex
##     <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
## 1    4.18       61.9     59.2    85.6
#Yes global life expectancy has changed significantly between 1925 and 2025. shows that the minimum life expectancy increased and the median and mean life expectancy are much higher in 2025, indicating that most countries now have life expectancy around 60 years or higher, max life expectancy is high
  1. Make a plot that shows the distribution of life expectancy for all countries in 1925 and 2025 (try using geom_density). What do you notice about the shift in life expectancy over time?
gapminder %>% 
  filter(year==1925|year==2025) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=lex,fill=as.factor(year))) +
  geom_density(alpha=0.5) +
  labs(title="life expectancy for all countries in 1925 and 2025",x = "life expectancy",fill = "yr") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1))
## Warning: Removed 13 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_density()`).

#shows that life expectancy has shifted to the right from 1925 to 2025 indicates that overall countries have higher life expectancy in 2025 compared to 1925 bc significant improvements in global health
  1. We are interested in the relationship between per capita GDP and life expectancy; i.e. does having more money help you live longer in 2025? Show this as a plot. (Suggestion! Remove Monaco as an extreme outlier.)
gapminder %>% 
  filter(year==2025,country!= "Monaco") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=gdp,y=lex))+
  geom_point()+
  labs(title = "relationship between per capita GDP and life expectancy in 2025",x="per capita GDP",y="life expectancy")+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1))
## Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_point()`).

#shown that money indeed does help you live longer, shown by the linear increase
  1. Which five countries have had the highest absolute GDP per capita growth over the past 50 years? Show this as a table. (Suggestion! Remove Monaco as an extreme outlier.)
gdp_growth<-gapminder %>% 
  filter(year%in%c(1975,2025),country!="Monaco")%>% 
  select(country,year,gdp)%>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from=year,values_from=gdp,names_prefix="gdp_")%>% 
  mutate(gdp_growth=gdp_2025-gdp_1975)%>% 
  slice_max(gdp_growth,n=5)
gdp_growth
## # A tibble: 5 × 4
##   country    gdp_1975 gdp_2025 gdp_growth
##   <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>
## 1 Singapore    12896.  137906.    125010.
## 2 Ireland      14336.  119406.    105071.
## 3 Luxembourg   30950.  131038.    100088.
## 4 Guyana        5071.   79371.     74300.
## 5 Norway       25513.   94896.     69382.
  1. How does per capita GDP growth compare between these same five countries over the past 50 years? Show this as a plot.
gapminder %>% 
  filter(country%in% gdp_growth$country,year>= 1975) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=year,y=gdp,color=country)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "per capita GDP growth in same 5 countries over the past 50 years",x = "yr",y = "GDP per Capita",color="Country") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1))

#all countries show an overall increase over the part 50 yrs, Luxembourg and Norway is stabilizing very slowly increasing

Table: Average GDP per year

gapminder
## # A tibble: 19,695 × 5
##    country      year     pop   gdp   lex

##  4 Afghanistan  1928 7442562 1157.  39.3

##  6 Afghanistan  1930 6888085 1186.  39.6
##  7 Afghanistan  1931 6736411 1201.  39.7
##  8 Afghanistan  1932 6662618 1216.  39.9
##  9 Afghanistan  1933 6662618 1231.  40.0
## 10 Afghanistan  1934 6662618 1247.  40.2

avg_gdp <- gapminder %>% 
  group_by(year) %>% 
  summarize(mean_gdp=mean(gdp,na.rm=T))
avg_gdp
## # A tibble: 101 × 2
##     year mean_gdp
##    <dbl>    <dbl>
##  1  1925    2912.
##  2  1926    2969.
##  3  1927    3027.
##  4  1928    3126.
##  5  1929    3196.
##  6  1930    3169.
##  7  1931    3087.
##  8  1932    3023.
##  9  1933    3096.
## 10  1934    3189.
## # ℹ 91 more rows
avg_gdp %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=year,y=mean_gdp))+
  geom_line()+
  labs(title="ave Global GDP per Capita",x = "yr",y = "ave GDP per Capita") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1))

#The average global GDP per capita has increased  between 1925 and 2025 indicating overall economic growth
